method_notes: Independent cross-check of two never-verified census populations (INDOOR_ARENA n=41; GREYHOUND_STADIUM n=18, all 18 capacity-review-flagged) plus the arena-adjacent sporting populations (ice hockey, basketball, athletics, tennis). Existing census venues were extracted programmatically from research/major-event-venues/uk-major-event-census-01/venues.json (642 venues; 41 INDOOR_ARENA, 18 GREYHOUND_STADIUM, 14 OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE) and every candidate below was name+city+alternative-name matched against the full 642 before being proposed, so nothing here is a known duplicate. REFERENCE POPULATIONS CHECKED: (1) National Arenas Association member list (fetched https://www.nationalarenasassociation.com/ - 23 members incl. one Irish); (2) Wikipedia List of indoor arenas in the United Kingdom (operational, under-construction and former sections); (3) Elite Ice Hockey League 2025-26 season venue list (10 venues); (4) Super League Basketball 2025-26 season venue list (9 venues); (5) Greyhound Board of Great Britain's own published licensed-track count (fetched https://www.gbgb.org.uk/racing/race-courses/ and https://www.gbgb.org.uk/rules-regulation/licensing/tracks/ - BOTH state 16 licensed stadia) cross-read against the named 16-track list and then confirmed track-by-track against each track's own official site; (6) UK greyhound openings/closures register maintained by the trade publication Greyhound Racing Times; (7) major permanent tennis tournament venues; (8) major athletics stadium population. VERDICT - INDOOR_ARENA: UNDERCOUNTED. The top-tier concert/entertainment arena estate is in fact substantially covered by the census as a whole - every NAA member arena except one, and every operational arena on the Wikipedia UK indoor arena list, reconciles to an existing census record - but several of them sit under a DIFFERENT venue_type and so are excluded from the 41 (P&J Live Aberdeen is CONVENTION_CENTRE; Brighton Centre, Swansea Building Society Arena, Alexandra Palace and Windsor Hall/Bournemouth are AUDITORIUM; Olympia London and The NEC are EXHIBITION_CENTRE; Royal Albert Hall is CONCERT_HALL; Emirates Arena Glasgow is OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE). Those are classification questions, not gaps, and are reported rather than re-listed here so as not to create duplicates. The REAL undercount is in the mid-scale (1,400-3,500 capacity) purpose-built sporting/entertainment arena tier: only 2 of the 9 Super League Basketball venues (Copper Box Arena, Playsport Arena) were in the census at all, and 1 of the 10 EIHL venues (Planet Ice Altrincham) was missing. Six operational arena-type venues and one under-construction arena are added below, plus one genuinely missing NAA member arena (East of England Arena, Peterborough) classified as MULTI_PURPOSE_EVENT_COMPLEX. VERDICT - GREYHOUND_STADIUM: MATERIALLY WRONG, NOT MERELY INCOMPLETE. GBGB itself states 16 licensed tracks; the census carries 18 active ones. Both surplus records are corrected below: Oxford Stadium closed on 3 April 2026 and is set CLOSED; Mildenhall Stadium's greyhound operation closed on 2 April 2026 while the site itself continues as a Spedeworth speedway/stock-car venue, so it is re-typed OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE and left OPERATIONAL rather than being falsely killed off or falsely preserved as an active track. All 18 existing greyhound records are re-listed (same canonical_name + city) because all 18 carried CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED and six carried no official URL at all; this pass supplies verified official URLs, addresses and fixture calendars. VERDICT - ICE HOCKEY: PLAUSIBLY_COMPLETE after one addition (9 of 10 EIHL venues already present). VERDICT - BASKETBALL: UNDERCOUNTED (5 of 9 top-tier venues added; 2 more fall below the 1,000 threshold and are excluded with cited figures). VERDICT - ATHLETICS: PLAUSIBLY_COMPLETE - Alexander Stadium, London Stadium, Manchester Regional Arena, Gateshead International Stadium, Crystal Palace NSC, Scotstoun Stadium, Cardiff International Sports Stadium and the indoor Emirates/Glasgow International Arena are all already in the census; no >=1,000 athletics venue was established as missing. VERDICT - TENNIS: UNDERCOUNTED BY ONE - AELTC, Queen's Club, Devonshire Park and Nottingham Tennis Centre were present; Edgbaston Priory Club (Lexus Birmingham Open) was not and is added. EXCLUSIONS ARE STATED EXPLICITLY in each excluded venue's absence and in the report: Surrey Sports Park (970), SGS College/WISE Arena Bristol (750) and Lee Valley Athletics Centre (500 permanent seats) are all below the 1,000 threshold; Dundonald International Ice Bowl is a public leisure ice rink and Belfast Giants training/secondary venue with no established spectator capacity; Edinburgh Arena at Edinburgh Park has planning consent but construction had NOT started as of July 2026, so no permitted operational_status honestly applies and it is deliberately omitted; the remaining Planet Ice community rinks (Blackburn, Bristol, Gillingham, Gosport, Hemel Hempstead, Leeds, Peterborough, Solihull, Uttoxeter, Widnes) were not evidenced as >=1,000 major-event infrastructure and are omitted. NO capacity, address, postcode, date or URL below is asserted without a URL that was actually fetched; where no figure was found the capacity is null with CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED rather than guessed. Latitude/longitude are null throughout by instruction.

venues.scale_description: CORRECTION TO EXISTING CENSUS RECORD. Oxford Stadium closed on 3 April 2026, ending its second spell of operation. It had reopened under a 10-year lease to Kevin Boothby with speedway returning 13 April 2022 and greyhound racing on 2 September 2022, after an earlier closure in December 2012. The immediate cause of the 2026 closure was the sudden withdrawal of the broadcaster funding its Saturday greyhound meetings; owner Paul Killen stated on 1-2 April 2026 that without a new sponsor the stadium would close that weekend. It is not among GBGB's 16 currently licensed tracks. The census previously carried it as OPERATIONAL with the note that oxfordstadium.co.uk was parked for sale - that parked domain is now explained: the operation has ended.
venues.no_public_calendar_reason: Venue closed on 3 April 2026; there is no forthcoming fixture calendar. No official web presence was identified.

evidence.note: Trade-press UK greyhound openings/closures register (page header states it is current as at 24 July 2026). Records 'April 3rd, 2026 OXFORD COWLEY (closure of second spell)' and the corresponding 'September 2nd, 2022 OXFORD Cowley (opens for second spell)'. This is the primary evidence for the CLOSED correction.

Independent contemporaneous news corroboration: reports the broadcaster's sudden exit, quotes owner Paul Killen that 'unless we get a new sponsor this weekend, the stadium will close', and confirms the venue hosted greyhound racing and banger/stock-car racing.

GBGB's own racecourses page states there are 16 GBGB licensed stadia. With the census carrying 18 active greyhound venues, this count is what prompted the track-by-track audit that identified Oxford and Mildenhall as the two surplus records.

Supplies the address (Sandy Lane, Cowley, Oxfordshire OX4 6LJ) and the 3,000 capacity, and documents the 2022 reopening. NOTE: this page had NOT been updated for the April 2026 closure at time of check and still described the stadium as operational - it is cited only for address/capacity/history, never for status.

venues.scale_description: CORRECTION TO EXISTING CENSUS RECORD - RECLASSIFICATION, NOT CLOSURE. Greyhound racing at this site (branded Suffolk Downs during part of its second spell) ceased on 2 April 2026, ending its second spell; the venue is no longer one of GBGB's 16 licensed tracks, so the census's GREYHOUND_STADIUM classification is now wrong. However the SITE IS NOT CLOSED: it opened in May 1975 for speedway, Spedeworth International owns the land, and speedway (Sundays, April-October) and stock-car racing continue. It is therefore re-typed OTHER_SPORTS_VENUE and left OPERATIONAL - it would be equally wrong to mark a live motorsport venue CLOSED as to leave a defunct greyhound track listed as an active one. Its greyhound history: racing began 21 September 1991, ceased 15 January 2018, resumed 8 February 2022, and ended 2 April 2026, with a significant fire on 30 July 2024 destroying a machinery building and damaging the bar and offices. No spectator capacity figure was found on any page fetched, so capacity is left null rather than guessed.
venues.no_public_calendar_reason: No first-party fixture calendar was retrievable. The Spedeworth International site returned only a splash/intro page with no dated fixtures at time of check, and no stadium-specific domain was identified. A calendar is likely to exist behind the splash page and should be re-probed.

evidence.note: Trade-press openings/closures register (current as at 24 July 2026) recording 'April 2nd, 2026 SUFFOLK DOWNS (aka MILDENHALL) (closure of second spell)' and the corresponding 'February 2nd, 2022 SUFFOLK DOWNS (aka MILDENHALL - opens for second spell)'. Primary evidence that the greyhound operation has ended.
